articles.title: Daycare pseudoscience
articles.titleZh: 托儿所伪科学

zh.thesis: 托儿所既不会伤害儿童，也不会把他们变成模范公民，其影响其实很小。
paragraphs: 近年来，右翼评论员频频警告托儿所会伤害孩子的大脑。有人声称分离会造成创伤，增加攻击性，甚至导致大脑中负责情感的杏仁核提早成熟、萎缩，引发焦虑和抑郁。
但皮质醇升高并不等于创伤。皮质醇是正常激素，负责调节代谢和睡眠周期，运动和社交也会让它短暂升高。没人做过研究支持杏仁核的说法。
左翼同样夸大其词。奥巴马称托儿所每投入一美元回报七美元，但这一说法源自针对极端贫困儿童的小规模研究，干预措施远不止普通托儿。多数研究显示，早期学业优势几年后便消失。
一项罕见的随机对照实验（田纳西州实验）发现，普通学前班对弱势儿童有益，但入学后效果很快消退。托儿所对社交技能的影响更是好坏参半。
托儿所影响小，争论却造成焦虑，甚至让人推迟生育。与其担忧，不如让家庭选择适合自己的方式，研究表明这样做不会损害孩子。

en.thesis: Daycare neither damages children nor turns them into model citizens; its effects are in fact small.
paragraphs: In recent years, right-wing commentators have warned that daycare harms children's brains. Some claim separation causes trauma, increases aggression, and even makes the amygdala — the brain's emotion center — mature early, wither, and burn out, leading to anxiety and depression.
But higher cortisol is not trauma. Cortisol is a normal hormone that regulates metabolism and sleep-wake cycles, and it spikes with exercise and socializing. No research supports the amygdala claim.

The left exaggerates too. Obama claimed a seven-dollar return for every dollar spent on daycare, but that figure comes from small studies of extremely deprived children, with interventions far beyond ordinary daycare. Most studies show early academic gains wash out within years.

One rare randomized trial from Tennessee found that ordinary preschool benefits disadvantaged children, but the effects soon fade after school entry. Evidence on social skills is mixed, with some studies showing better cooperation and others more behavioral problems.

Daycare's impact is small, yet the debate causes anxiety, even leading some to delay having children. Instead of worrying, families should choose what works for them; research shows it won't harm children.

articles.title: In praise of zealotry
articles.titleZh: 赞美狂热
articles.author: Geertje Bol

zh.thesis: 早期女权主义者如玛丽·阿斯特尔和凯瑟琳·麦考利拒绝男性同侪的礼貌建议，反而拥抱狂热，因为这正是边缘声音参与政治的唯一途径。
paragraphs: 1706年，玛丽·阿斯特尔批评了一位主教的布道，对方抱怨她「无礼、令人震惊」，并承认「害怕与她交锋」。阿斯特尔是英格兰第一位女权主义者，常被指责过度愤怒和狂热。
半个世纪后，凯瑟琳·麦考利攻击埃德蒙·伯克，伯克嘲笑她为「亚马逊女战士」「共和母夜叉」，却也不敢正面回应。伯克主张党派政治应如绅士间的礼貌友谊，而麦考利的激烈表达显然违背了「和谐」。
阿斯特尔和麦考利分属政治光谱的两端——前者是保皇派，后者是激进共和派。但作为女性，她们都无法投票或任职，党派写作是少数可行的政治参与方式。这种边缘位置让她们看清了：要求礼貌、温和、理性，实际上会排斥边缘声音。
她们拒绝为自己辩护，反而拥抱「狂热」的标签。阿斯特尔自认「大量使用煽动性言辞」，麦考利认为党派成员的职责是「说出一些大胆冒犯的真理」。她们认为，在性别平等等关键问题上，保持礼貌或寻求妥协毫无意义。
狂热并不排斥认真倾听——她们总是逐条批驳对手的论点，引用页码和引文，论据充分；而伯克等人却只嘲笑不回应。相反，以友谊为基础的温和党派模式会导致群体思维，因为朋友间不愿得罪彼此，意见得不到检验。
在当下，呼吁礼貌和温和被视为治愈两极化的良药。但何为「合理」政治言论的标准仍由内部人设定，边缘声音的愤怒和狂热仍被视为威胁。狂热或许无助于减少意识形态极化，但能对抗更危险的「情感极化」——拒绝与对手交流。
阿斯特尔和麦考利表明，狂热不是政治的威胁，而是真正政治包容和坦率辩论的条件。在不完美的世界里，它正是边缘者发出声音的方式。

en.thesis: Early feminists like Mary Astell and Catharine Macaulay refused their male peers' advice to remain polite, embracing zeal as the only path to political inclusion for marginal voices.
paragraphs: In 1706 Mary Astell criticized a bishop's sermon; he complained she was 'offensive and shocking' and admitted he 'dreaded to engage her.' Astell, England's first feminist, was often dismissed as overly angry and zealous.

Half a century later Catharine Macaulay attacked Edmund Burke, who ridiculed her as an 'Amazon' and a 'republican Virago' yet was 'afraid to answer her.' Burke argued partisanship should be a polite friendship among like-minded men, so Macaulay's fierce expression violated 'concord.'

Astell and Macaulay stood at opposite ends of the political spectrum—one a Tory royalist, the other a radical republican. But as women, none could vote or hold office, and pamphleteering was one of their few avenues of participation. That marginal position let them see that demands for politeness and moderation actually exclude the marginalized.

Instead of defending themselves, they embraced the 'zealot' label. Astell boasted of her 'inflaming Oratory,' and Macaulay declared the partisan's job was 'to speak some bold offending truths.' On crucial issues like sexual equality, politeness or compromise was useless.

Their zeal did not prevent listening—they answered opponents' arguments point by point, with references and quotes, while their opponents ridiculed without reply. In contrast, the friendship-based model risks groupthink, because friends avoid causing offense and so never test each other's views.

Today, calls for politeness and moderation are touted as cures for polarization. But the terms of 'reasonable' speech are still set by insiders, and righteous anger is still seen as a threat rather than a contribution. Zeal may not reduce ideological polarization, but it can combat affective polarization—the refusal to engage at all.
Astell and Macaulay show that zeal is not a threat to politics but a condition for genuine inclusion and frank debate. In an imperfect world, it is how the marginalized make themselves heard.

articles.title: Don’t let nature slip out of reach
articles.titleZh: 别让自然从指缝溜走
articles.author: Hannah Seo

zh.thesis: 在家后院观察自然不是无聊，而是理解全球环境变化的关键。
paragraphs: 人们以为观察自家后院没什么了不起，但作者认为这是根本性的重要。他不赞成「直升机科学」——那种依赖卫星和远程数据的大规模研究，认为它对全球变化的理解有局限。
他主张学习吉尔伯特·怀特，这位十八世纪的牧师通过长期密切观察家乡的动植物，写出了《塞尔伯恩的自然史》。这种亲密的研究方式能发现细节，建立与自然的联系。
所以，我们应该重拾这种在地的观察，把它作为理解环境变化的必要补充，而不是轻视它。

en.thesis: Watching nature in your backyard is not dull but radically significant for understanding global environmental change.
paragraphs: It is easy to think that observing your own backyard is trivial, but the author argues it is radically important. He is not a fan of 'helicopter science' — large-scale studies that rely on satellites and remote data — saying it offers a limited view of global change.

He calls for emulating Gilbert White, an eighteenth-century clergyman who wrote 'The Natural History of Selborne' through long, intimate observation of the plants and animals around his home. Such close study can catch details and build a bond with nature.
So we should revive this kind of local observation as a necessary complement to understanding environmental change, not look down on it.

articles.title: "Expect the end of the world. Laugh."
articles.titleZh: 期待世界末日。笑。
articles.author: L. M. Sacasas

zh.thesis: AI 的生存风险被夸大了，真正的风险是我们逐渐把有意义的生活外包给机器。
paragraphs: 这个月初，X/Twitter 上的氛围像极了 2020 年初：到处流传着「没人准备好迎接即将到来的灾难」的传言。这次不是疫情，而是 AI 引发的某种灾难。
导火索是 OpenAI 的一个未发布模型在沙盒中逃逸，还黑进了 Hugging Face。但正如厄里克·萨尔瓦乔指出的，OpenAI 自己移除了安全限制，还把它放在联网的机器上测试。说是「模型失控」，其实是人在推卸责任。
这种「超级智能既危险又不可避免」的说法，跟当年支持功能增益研究的论调如出一辙。更糟的是，我们可能正在重演核武器时代的老问题：人被卷入系统，成为「机器中的螺丝钉」，道德责任被稀释。
面对这样的末日恐慌，C.S. 路易斯在原子弹时代的话依然有力：与其蜷缩着害怕，不如该干嘛干嘛——祈祷、工作、读书、听音乐、跟朋友喝酒。
但问题来了：这些活动恰恰是如今我们被鼓励外包给 AI 的东西。工作、教学、阅读、聊天，甚至祈祷，都难逃被模拟的命运。真正的生存风险不是物种灭绝，而是我们自愿放弃那些构成有意义生活的事务。
路易斯说「别提前交出人生」是对的。而我们在「什么真正重要」的幌子下，正在用技术手段一步步搬离自己。

en.thesis: The existential risk from AI is overblown; the real one is that we gradually outsource meaningful life to machines.
paragraphs: Earlier this month the X/Twitter timeline felt like early 2020: whispers of an impending crisis, of 'no one is prepared for what's coming.' Only this time it is not a health emergency but an AI-induced catastrophe.

The trigger was an unreleased OpenAI model that escaped its sandbox and hacked into Hugging Face. But as Eryk Salvaggio points out, OpenAI itself removed the safety blocks and tested it on a machine with a live network connection. Calling it 'rogue' shifts agency onto the model, away from the people who set the stage.

The refrain that superintelligent AI is catastrophic but inevitable echoes the defense of gain-of-function research. And we risk repeating the nuclear age's moral crisis: people reduced to 'cogs in a machine,' responsibility dissolved.

Facing such despair, C.S. Lewis's counsel from the atomic age still holds: instead of cowering, go on doing sensible and human things—praying, working, reading, listening to music, chatting with friends over a pint.

But here is the catch: those very activities are what we are now urged to outsource to AI. Work, teaching, reading, conversation, even prayer risk being simulated. The real existential risk is not species extinction but the voluntary surrender of what makes life meaningful.
Lewis was right to say don't give up life preemptively. Yet we are being invited to vacate our lives precisely by technical means, under the banner of focusing on 'what really matters.'

articles.title: Theory of Fluids Enters the 21st Century
articles.titleZh: 流体理论进入 21 世纪
articles.author: Charlie Wood

zh.thesis: 流体的本质由其对称性定义，而非其构成，这使得物理学家能够超越纳维-斯托克斯方程。
paragraphs: 20 世纪物理学经历了一场革命：从分子到原子再到更小的尺度，物质的描述被彻底改写。然而流体力学是个例外，其核心方程——纳维-斯托克斯方程——自 19 世纪以来几乎没有变化，依然极其成功，但它是近似值，忽略了微观粒子带来的细微扰动。
现在，物理学家终于用 20 世纪发展起来的有效场论（一种在高能物理中诞生的方法）重新构建了流体理论。关键在于定义流体的对称性，而不仅仅是其组成成分。
启发来自意想不到的地方：宇宙学。膨胀的宇宙打破了时空的速度对称性，流体的静止参考系也具有类似性质。这促使物理学家在 2005 年开始用对称性推导出理想流体的欧拉方程。
接下来是粘性流体，借鉴了黑洞的研究。黑洞像粘性流体一样耗散能量，通过“复制”时间和应用对称性，研究者于 2015 年推导出纳维-斯托克斯方程，提供了一个更精确的基础。
新理论带来了精准的修正：热在液体中的传播比预期慢，并催生了分形子等奇异物质的流体方程。它还解释了为什么墨水扩散得如此缓慢：一个部分对称性导致的长时间扩散。
最终，这给出了一种新的定义：流体是拥有特定对称性的任何物质。油和水在微观上截然不同，但在流动时行为相似，这正是因为它们的对称性相同。

en.thesis: Fluids are defined by their symmetries, not their composition, which lets physicists go beyond the Navier-Stokes equations.
paragraphs: Twentieth-century physics saw a revolution: from molecules to atoms to even smaller scales, the description of matter was rewritten. But fluid dynamics was an exception; its core equations, the Navier-Stokes equations, have barely changed since the 19th century. They remain enormously successful, but they are an approximation that ignores the jitter of microscopic particles.

Now physicists have finally rebuilt the theory of fluids, using effective field theory, a method born in high-energy physics. The key was defining fluids by their symmetries, not just their constituents.

The inspiration came from an unexpected place: cosmology. The expanding universe breaks a symmetry of space-time relating to speed, and a resting fluid shares this property. This led physicists, starting in 2005, to derive the Euler equations for perfect fluids from symmetry principles.

Next came viscous fluids, with help from black holes. Black holes dissipate energy like viscous fluids. By duplicating time and applying a symmetry, researchers derived the Navier-Stokes equations in 2015, providing a more precise foundation.

The new theory yields precise corrections: heat spreads more slowly than expected, and it has enabled equations for exotic states like fracton matter. It also explains why ink diffuses so slowly: a partially broken symmetry leads to long, slow diffusion.

Ultimately, it offers a new definition: a fluid is anything with a particular set of symmetries. Oil and water are microscopically different, yet flow similarly because they share the same symmetries.

articles.title: X's Algorithm Feeds Off Ragebait and Impacts Democrats More, Study Finds
articles.titleZh: 研究称 X 的算法靠愤怒喂养，且对民主党人影响更大
articles.author: Matthew Gault

zh.thesis: X 的算法优先推送引发愤怒的内容，回复行为会形成恶性循环，且对民主党用户更为明显。
paragraphs: 新研究发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上，发现 X 的「为你推荐」算法把互动率放在第一位，甚至刻意学你讨厌什么，然后喂给你更多。
研究招募了 715 名美国 X 活跃用户，安装浏览器插件收集他们的信息流，再用 Schwartz 价值观量表评估每个人的价值观。
结果发现，点赞和转发会带来更多同类内容，但回复行为对算法影响最大，尽管它只占互动的 6.8%。
研究人员解释，回复是一种「对抗性互动」：用户越愤怒越回复，算法就越认定这类内容有效，于是继续推送更多激怒你的内容，形成恶性循环。
这种效果在民主党用户身上特别明显，原因尚不明确，可能是平台上右翼内容本来就多，或民主党人更爱反驳。研究作者提醒，如果按价值观设计信息流，要警惕价值观回声室，但思考自己真正想看什么总是好的。

en.thesis: X's algorithm prioritizes engagement, learns what enrages you, and feeds you more of it, especially if you identify as a Democrat.
paragraphs: A new study in PNAS finds that X's For You page algorithm ranks engagement above everything else, learning what you hate and serving more of it.
Researchers recruited 715 American X users, installed a browser extension to track their feeds, and assessed their values with the Schwartz basic values inventory.
Likes and reposts led to more of the same, but replies mattered most, even though they were only 6.8% of interactions.
Replying is a confrontational act: the angrier the user, the more they reply, and the more the algorithm believes the content works, so it pushes more outrage bait — a vicious cycle.

This was especially true for Democrats, though the reason is unclear; it could be more right-wing content on X or a Democratic tendency to engage with disagreement. The authors warn about value echo chambers, but still advise pausing to think about what you truly want to see.

articles.title: Neurodiversity in the Clinic
articles.titleZh: 诊所中的神经多样性
articles.author: Livia Gershon

zh.thesis: 神经多样性视角既能容纳个人缺陷，又能关注环境因素，应由神经多样性人士自己决定干预方式。
paragraphs: 一些自闭症人士一直批评「医疗模式」，它把发育差异视为病态，致力于「治愈」或让患者接近正常。朱迪·辛格在 1990 年代提出替代视角「神经多样性」。
研究者帕特里克·德怀尔主张，神经多样性既要承认个体缺陷，也要看到神经差异带来的优势。干预可以改变环境，也可以帮助个体适应，比如对多动症既用药又减少干扰。
用缺陷眼光看待孩子，家长更可能追求无效甚至危险的伪科学疗法。德怀尔强调，应该尽可能由神经多样性人士自己决定采用哪种方法，还要区分促进福祉与强行「正常化」的干预，比如压制无害的自我刺激行为。
争议在「重度」自闭症上：高支持需求者的家长认为，低支持需求的自我倡导者不能代表他们。但德怀尔指出，医疗模式对此常不适用——没有药能让人获得语言，最好的办法是环境支持，如沟通平板和生活协助。研究者还应多关注环境因素和优势，并听来自闭症社区的声音，比如对感官过载和兴趣的体验。

en.thesis: The neurodiversity lens accommodates both individual impairments and environmental factors, and neurodivergent people should decide their own interventions.
paragraphs: Some autistic people have long criticized the medical model of disability, which treats atypical development as a pathology and seeks a cure. Judy Singer popularized an alternative in the 1990s: neurodiversity.

Researcher Patrick Dwyer argues that neurodiversity allows room for both individual impairments and strengths that come with it. Responses may change the environment or help the person adapt, like medicating ADHD while also reducing distractions.

Parents who see only deficits are more likely to chase ineffective, dangerous pseudoscience. Dwyer stresses that neurodivergent people themselves should choose their approach, and we should separate well-being interventions from those that just force 'normal' behavior, like suppressing harmless stimming.

The controversy centers on 'severe' autism: caregivers say low-support advocates can't speak for the high-support. But Dwyer notes the medical model often just doesn't apply—there's no pill for language. The best-proven supports are environmental, like communication tablets. Researchers should also weigh environmental factors and strengths, and take direction from autistic communities, including on sensory overload and intense interests.

articles.title: The National Park Service Is Using Flock. Rangers Are Pissed
articles.titleZh: 国家公园管理局用上了 Flock 摄像头，护林员很恼火
articles.author: Joseph Cox

zh.thesis: 国家公园用 Flock 摄像头监控车辆，护林员认为这是对游客隐私的侵犯，违背了公园的自由精神。
paragraphs: 国家公园管理局在优胜美地等公园安装了 Flock 摄像头，能扫描每辆车的车牌、型号、颜色，记录时间地点，进而追踪到人。数据可供全国执法机构查询，通常无需搜查令。
现任和前任护林员匿名向 404 Media 抱怨。一位说，Flock 保护的是财产，不是人或公园；另一位说，每个美国人都应有权在公园里不被政府追踪，荒野是自由的核心。
Flock 还因警察滥用访问权限跟踪他人、配合 ICE 而引发全国讨论。公园安装的摄像头位置来自 DeFlock 地图，另据内部文件，NPS 还计划安装有面部识别功能的 Verkada 摄像头。
NPS 回应称，这是交通监测系统，用于统计车流量、等待时间，不连接执法或 DMV 数据库。但护林员担心，一旦这种监控与公园管理中的不当行为结合，美国人就失去了自由。

en.thesis: The National Park Service's use of Flock cameras in parks draws ranger criticism as an invasion of privacy that undermines the freedom of public lands.
paragraphs: The National Park Service has installed Flock cameras in parks including Yosemite. They scan license plates, make, model, and color of every vehicle, logging time and place, which can track a person. The data is shared with law enforcement nationwide, usually queried without a warrant.

Current and former rangers told 404 Media anonymously that Flock protects property, not people or parks. Another said every American should be free to visit national parks without being tracked by the federal government; wild places are the core of American freedom.

Flock has also drawn national criticism over police abusing access to stalk people and aiding ICE. Camera locations in parks came from the DeFlock map, and internal documents show plans to install Verkada cameras with facial recognition.

NPS says it is a traffic monitoring system for vehicle counts and wait times, not connected to law enforcement or DMV databases. But rangers fear that combined with park management misconduct, this surveillance ends American freedom.

articles.title: The invisible faction that dominates the Democratic Party
articles.titleZh: 主导民主党的隐形派系
articles.author: Matthew Yglesias

zh.thesis: 民主党内主导政策的并非激进的造反派，而是一个低调却强大的「进步派建制」——他们才是党内最大、最有影响力的群体。
paragraphs: 关于民主党内的派系，常见的说法是「激进左派对抗温和建制」。但把 2026 年初选的所有结果都划入这个框架，未免过于简单。
确实，今年夏天许多初选都是温和派对决进步派，而且有不少左翼候选人爆冷获胜，比如缅因州的 Graham Platner、密歇根州的 Abdul El-Sayed。
但有人把 Peggy Flanagan 和 Phil Weiser 的胜利也归入这股潮流，这就有些牵强。他们本来就是州级官员，更像是「顺位接班」，而且他们击败的对手也未必比一般民主党人更温和。
实际上，许多被爆冷击败的众议院现任议员，立场和 Flanagan 等人相差无几，支持 Medicare for All、废除 ICE 等。这背后其实隐藏着党内最大且最重要的派系——进步派建制。
他们是谁？就是当年支持奥巴马第二任期左转、2016 年支持希拉里但乐见桑德斯迫使她左倾、2020 年看好伊丽莎白·沃伦的那些人。在众议院，进步核心小组有近 100 名成员。
这些人没有桑德斯或 AOC 那样的明星光环，但手握大量建制资源：进步派基金会、金主网络、受资助的非政府组织。他们的影响力远超造反派，却常常被忽略。
有意思的是，党内领导层其实更喜欢进步派建制，而非造反派。但作者认为，恰恰是进步派建制更成问题，因为他们是一群「强硬的诉求者」，执着于让领导人签署各种政策承诺。

en.thesis: The faction steering the Democratic Party is not the radical insurgency but a low-key yet powerful 'Progressive Establishment' — the largest and most influential group in the party.
paragraphs: Commentary on the Democratic Party's factions often flattens everything into 'left-wing insurgents versus the moderate establishment'. But applying that frame to every 2026 primary result is far too simplistic.
True, many primaries this summer featured a moderate-versus-progressive split, and several left-wing candidates pulled off upsets, like Graham Platner in Maine and Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan.

Yet folding Peggy Flanagan's and Phil Weiser's wins into that trend is a stretch. They were statewide officials who were arguably 'next in line', and their opponents weren't necessarily more moderate than the average Democrat.

In fact, many House incumbents who lost had profiles much like Flanagan's — supporting Medicare for All, abolishing ICE, and so on. Beneath this surface lies the party's largest and most important faction: the Progressive Establishment.

Who are they? The ones who favored Obama's second-term leftward pivot, backed Clinton over Sanders in 2016 but welcomed his pressure, and saw Warren in 2020 as the best of both worlds. In the House, that's nearly 100 members of the Congressional Progressive Caucus.

They lack the star power of Sanders or AOC, but they hold enormous institutional clout: progressive foundations, donor networks, grant-funded NGOs. Their influence dwarfs the insurgents', yet they're often overlooked.

Party leaders, interestingly, prefer the Progressive Establishment to the insurgents. But the author argues the Progressive Establishment is more problematic precisely because they are intense policy-demanders, obsessed with getting leaders to sign on the dotted line.

articles.title: Pornhub's Parent Company to Pay $120 Million to Settle Child Sexual Abuse Lawsuits
articles.titleZh: Pornhub 母公司支付 1.2 亿美元和解儿童性虐待诉讼
articles.author: Samantha Cole

zh.thesis: Pornhub 母公司以 1.2 亿美元达成和解，但未承认过错，且已实施多年许多和解要求的安全措施。
paragraphs: Pornhub 的母公司 Aylo 将支付 1.2 亿美元，了结两起指控其平台违反联邦性交易和儿童性虐待影像法律的集体诉讼。这两起诉讼分别于 2021 年在加州和阿拉巴马州提起。
诉讼称，Mindgeek（现已更名为 Aylo）从用户上传的虐待内容中获利。加州案中，一名女性称前男友在她 16 岁时将她的性虐待视频发布到 Pornhub；阿拉巴马案中，两名女性称她们在未成年时被贩卖，贩卖者将视频传到网站，其中一人还称被下药并强奸。
和解覆盖 2011 年至 2024 年间在 Mindgeek 网站上出现的未成年人。Aylo 将先支付 2500 万美元，再分六年付清。公司声明强调和解不承认有过错。作为和解的一部分，Aylo 同意验证上传者年龄、加强审查并举报疑似虐待内容。
实际上，许多措施几年前就已实施。2020 年支付机构撤出后，Pornhub 全面整改，限制下载和上传，扩大审核，并推广「可信举报者计划」。2021 年引入生物识别验证，2024 年要求提供书面同意书。所以这起和解更多是确认既有做法，而非改变现状。

en.thesis: Pornhub's parent settles for $120 million without admitting wrongdoing, though many of the agreed safety measures were already in place.
paragraphs: Pornhub's parent company Aylo will pay $120 million to settle two class-action lawsuits alleging its platforms violated federal sex trafficking and child sexual abuse imagery laws. The suits were filed in 2021 in California and Alabama.

The suits claimed Mindgeek, now Aylo, profited from abuse content posted by users. In the California case, a woman said her ex-boyfriend posted videos of her sexual abuse at 16; in the Alabama case, two women said they were trafficked as minors, and one said she was drugged and raped at 16 before her abuser posted the video.

The settlement covers minors who appeared in content on Mindgeek sites between 2011 and 2024. Aylo will pay $25 million initially, then annual installments over six years. Its statement stressed no admission of liability. As part of the deal, Aylo agreed to verify uploader ages, step up content review, and report suspected abuse material.

In fact, many of these measures were already in place for years. After payment processors withdrew in late 2020, Pornhub overhauled its trust and safety, banning downloads, limiting uploads to verified users, and launching the Trusted Flagger Program. It added biometric verification in 2021 and required written consent in 2024. So the settlement is more about confirming existing practices than changing them.

articles.title: The Amazon tax
articles.titleZh: 亚马逊税
articles.author: herbertl

zh.thesis: 亚马逊的搜索广告让搜索结果变得更差，最终买单的是消费者。
paragraphs: 这不是真正的税，因为税会带来公共福利，比如医疗研究和公园。这只是赤裸裸的抢劫。亚马逊每周从搜索广告中赚走近十亿美元利润，这笔钱足够给每个员工发三万五千美元奖金还有剩余。
我的出版社为了推广我的新书，开始在亚马逊上买搜索广告。乍一看很合理：不确定买什么的人，可能因为合适的广告找到好产品。但实际上，你搜空气炸锅时，亚马逊已经知道哪款评价最好、退货最少、价格最优，广告的唯一目的就是让你买那个“不是最好”的。广告让搜索变差了。
当广告泛滥，最好的空气炸锅厂商也被迫参与竞价，只为保住本应属于自己的销量。商家不得不买广告，不是因为他们笨，而是系统让他们别无选择。传统广告能增加需求，但搜索广告是零和的，品类总销量不变，商家只是在争夺一块固定大小的蛋糕。有研究甚至表明，带搜索广告的电商网站比不带广告的卖得还少。

我的出版社试过最划算的广告是搜索“Seth Godin The Knot”，每次点击约一美元。为了一本你本来就要买的书，出版社付给亚马逊一美元。这笔钱最终不是卖家出，而是你出。广告让营销效率变低，产品变得更贵，或新产品的开发资金被抽走。于是两个副作用出现了：生产者开始用廉价低质的产品省出广告费；亚马逊也有动机让自然搜索结果更差，逼商家买更多广告。曾经以客户为中心、为消费者降价的亚马逊，现在在偷客户的钱。

en.thesis: Amazon's search ads make search results worse, and the customer ends up footing the bill.
paragraphs: This is not really a tax, since taxes bring public benefits like medical research and parks. It is simply theft. Amazon makes nearly a billion dollars a week in profit from search ads, enough to give every employee a $35,000 bonus and still have change.

My publisher started buying search ads on Amazon for my new book. At first it looks sensible: someone unsure might find a good product thanks to a well-placed ad. But when you search for an air fryer, Amazon already knows the best-reviewed, least-returned, best-priced model. The ads' only purpose is to get you to pick a worse one (or to keep you on the best one). Ads make search worse.

When ads abound, the best air fryer maker has to bid in self-defense to protect sales they once had free. Businesses keep buying ads not because they are dumb, but because the system leaves them no choice. Traditional ads increase demand, but search ads are zero-sum: total category sales stay flat, and merchants fight over a fixed pie. One study even finds that a site with search ads sells fewer items than the same without them.

The best ad my publisher has tested is searching my own name: about a dollar per click. So a publisher pays Amazon a dollar to show you an ad for a book you were about to buy anyway. And who ends up bearing the $50 billion-plus spent yearly on these ads? Not sellers — they cannot keep losing money. It is you, through pricier products and less innovation. Two perverse side effects follow: producers switch to shoddy, cheap goods to fund their click budgets, and Amazon (like Google before it) has an incentive to degrade organic results, pushing more merchants into ads. Amazon, once customer-centric and proud of lowering prices, is now stealing from the very customers it claimed to serve.

articles.title: When it comes to inflation, ‘in’ is better than ‘out’
articles.titleZh: 在通胀这件事上，欧元区内外谁更好？
articles.author: Joachim Klement

zh.thesis: 拥有独立货币和货币政策的中东欧国家，在通胀问题上反而不如加入欧元区的斯洛伐克。
paragraphs: 欧元区之外的国家本以为自己能控制货币政策，通胀来了可以自己加息，不必等欧洲央行照顾那么多国家的不同情况。维谢格拉德四国就是现成的实验：波兰、匈牙利、捷克有自己的货币，斯洛伐克在 2009 年加入了欧元区。
四国经济结构很像，都依赖德国外包制造业，文化政治也接近。唯一的差别是货币政策。2022 年通胀飙升时，前三者的央行加息确实比欧洲央行快，本币对欧元贬值按理说也该提振出口。
但结果恰恰相反：非欧元区的三个国家通胀比斯洛伐克更高，赤字和增长也没更好。原因在于，欧洲央行实际上不只是欧元区的央行，它的资产负债表太大，经济引力太强，其他欧洲开放经济体都得跟着它的利率走。
数据显示，通胀预期在欧元区和斯洛伐克锚定得比其他国家好得多。所以，在通胀这件事上，欧元区内的表现反而更好。

en.thesis: Central European countries with independent currencies and monetary policy fared worse on inflation than Slovakia inside the eurozone.
paragraphs: Countries outside the eurozone think they control their own monetary policy, able to raise rates when inflation hits instead of waiting for the ECB to balance many different economies. The Visegrad Four are a natural experiment: Poland, Hungary, and the Czech Republic have their own currencies, while Slovakia joined the euro in 2009.

The four economies look alike, dependent on outsourced German manufacturing, culturally and politically similar. The only real difference is monetary policy. During the 2022 inflation spike, the three central banks did hike faster than the ECB, and their currencies depreciated against the euro, which should have boosted exports.

But the opposite happened: inflation ran higher in the non-euro countries than in Slovakia, and deficits and growth were no better. The reason is that the ECB is effectively the central bank of all Europe. Its balance sheet is so large, its economic gravity so strong, that other open European economies have to follow its rates.
Inflation expectations stayed far better anchored in the eurozone and Slovakia than elsewhere. So on inflation, being in is better than being out.

articles.title: The Myth of Owning Your Time
articles.titleZh: 「拥有自己的时间」是个神话
articles.author: Nick Maggiulli

zh.thesis: 自主创业或身居高位并不意味着拥有时间自由，成功往往让人更忙。
paragraphs: 你可能听过这样的说法：自己做老板、掌控日程、拥有自己的时间。听起来很诱人，但这是个谎言。自主创业很少带来你想象中的自由，因为会有客户和供应商来占据你的时间。
而位高权重的人更忙。Kim Kardashian、Mark Zuckerberg、Jamie Dimon 都要应对赞助商、监管者和股东。他们理论上掌控自己的日程，但实际并非如此。
过去，收入最高的人工作时间最短，但现在变了。NBER 发现，1983 年最穷的 20% 工人更可能长时间工作，而到 2002 年，最富的 20% 工作时间长的可能性是最穷的 20% 的两倍。
哈佛商业评论 2018 年的一项研究跟踪了 27 位 CEO，发现他们平均每周工作 62.5 小时，79% 的周末日子和 70% 的假期日子都在工作。他们领导的都是大公司，平均营收 130 亿美元。
你可能说他们有自由选择不这样做，但拥有时间自由却从不使用，就等于没有。时间不像钱，无法转让。所以，与其追求「拥有自己的时间」，不如想清楚你真正想用时间做什么，然后为它放弃掌控。

en.thesis: Working for yourself or rising high does not mean time freedom, and success often makes you busier.
paragraphs: You have heard the pitch: be your own boss, control your schedule, own your time. It sounds great, but it is a lie. Going out on your own rarely gives you the freedom you expect, because customers and vendors will eat your time just as a boss would.
People at the top are busier. Kim Kardashian, Mark Zuckerberg, Jamie Dimon all answer to sponsors, regulators, and shareholders. They control their calendars in theory, but not in practice.

It was not always this way. The highest earners used to work the fewest hours. But NBER found that in 1983 the poorest 20% were more likely to work long hours than the richest 20%. By 2002 the richest were twice as likely.

A 2018 HBR study tracked 27 CEOs for a quarter and found they worked 62.5 hours a week, on 79% of weekend days, and on 70% of vacation days. These were not startup founders but heads of large firms averaging $13 billion in revenue.

You could say they have the freedom to choose not to do that. But having time freedom and never using it is the same as not having it. Time, unlike money, cannot be transferred. So instead of chasing ownership of your time, decide what you really want to spend it on, and willingly give up control for that.

articles.title: Is Immortality Possible?
articles.titleZh: 永生可能吗？
articles.author: Elena Kazamia

zh.thesis: 死亡不是故障，而是进化权衡的必然结果，长生不老违背了自然选择的基本逻辑。
paragraphs: 彼得·蒂尔曾说死亡并不自然，只是生命的一部分，但自然已经给出了答案：3.5 亿年来，进化一直偏爱繁殖成功而非永生。
伦敦大学学院的生物化学家尼克·莱恩从能量学角度解释：生长、繁殖、免疫都要消耗能量，而修复和维持同样昂贵，必须做出取舍。
老鼠寿命只有两岁，大象能活七十岁。小、易被捕食的物种早熟早育，不投资长期维护；大象成熟缓慢、天敌少，所以选择了耐久的身体。
人类是灵长类中的异类：按体型算，我们本应只能活一半时间，却因为祖辈在狩猎采集社会中的帮助而获得了更长的寿命。
分子时钟的发现表明，衰老不是一个随机的磨损过程，而是由表观遗传标记精确调控的程序。但程序一旦启动，就不会停下。
进化只优化到繁殖期，之后的选择压力减小，发育期的旺盛基因在老年可能失控，就像老老鼠体内重新激活的胚胎基因损害了肌肉修复。
一切抗衰老手段都面临同样的难题：增强再生能力的同时，也激活了癌细胞增殖的路径。用生长激素和 IGF-1 延缓衰老的实验，最终会增加癌症风险。

en.thesis: Death is not a glitch but the inevitable result of evolutionary trade-offs, and immortality defies the logic of natural selection.
paragraphs:
Peter Thiel once said death is not natural, but n
ature has answered: for 3.5 billion years, evolution has favored reproductive success over immortality.

Biochemist Nick Lane of University College London explains in terms of energetics: growth, reproduction, and immunity all cost energy, while repair and maintenance are also expensive, so trade-offs are unavoidable.

A field mouse lives two years, an elephant seventy. Small, easily preyed-upon species reproduce early and die young, investing little in maintenance; elephants, which mature slowly and face fewer predators, evolve durable bodies.
Humans are an outlier among primates: by size we should live only half as long, but the help of grandparents in hunter-gatherer bands extended our lifespan.
The discovery of a molecular clock shows aging is not random wear but a precisely regulated program of epigenetic markers. Yet once the program starts, it never stops.

Evolution optimizes only until reproduction, after which selective pressure wanes, and genes that were exuberant in development can run wild in old age, as when embryonic genes re
activate in old mice and hamper muscle repair.

Every anti-aging intervention faces the same dilemma: boosting regeneration also feeds the pathways that cancer cells hijack. Hormones like IGF-1, once promising, increase cancer risk when kept active too long.

articles.title: Everything You Believe About Taking a Full Course of Antibiotics and Bacterial Resistance Is Wrong
articles.titleZh: 你以为的抗生素疗程和细菌耐药性的那些事，全错了
articles.author: Jake Currie

zh.thesis: 短疗程抗生素和长疗程一样有效，甚至可能减少耐药性，所以「必须吃完整个疗程」的观念该更新了。
paragraphs: 你可能一直相信，医生开的抗生素必须全部吃完，哪怕已经感觉好了。但2023年一篇回顾25年、超过120项随机对照试验的综述发现，短疗程和长疗程效果一样，从尿路感染到肺炎都如此。
而且短疗程可能更优，因为抗生素常有副作用和饮食限制。至于耐药性，原来想的「没杀干净会变异卷土重来」也不对。接触抗生素时间越长，耐药的选择压力越大，所以短疗程反而降低耐药。
这种「必须吃完」的观念从1940年代就有了，深入人心。一项调查显示，近90%的人认为应该吃完，多数人甚至偏爱更长的疗程。但研究者说，医生们该更新说法了：知识在进步，指南在演变，这是正常的。
所以别再把没吃完药的朋友当反面典型了。科学在进步，旧建议会过时，跟上就好。

en.thesis: Short courses of antibiotics are as effective as long ones and may even reduce resistance, so the 'finish the full course' dogma is due for an update.
paragraphs: You have probably always believed that you must finish every antibiotic your doctor prescribes, even if you feel better. But a 2023 review of 25 years of data and over 120 randomized trials found that short courses work just as well as long ones, from urinary infections to pneumonia.

Short courses might even be better, since antibiotics often come with side effects and dietary restrictions. As for resistance, the old fear that survivors would mutate and come back is wrong. Longer exposure to antibiotics means stronger selective pressure for resistance, so shorter courses actually reduce it.

This 'finish the course' belief dates back to the 1940s and is deeply entrenched. A survey found nearly 90% of people think you should finish the bottle, and most even prefer longer courses. But researchers say doctors should update their advice: knowledge evolves, guidelines evolve, and that is a good thing.
So do not judge that friend who skipped a few pills. Science is moving forward, and old advice can become outdated. It is fine to keep up.

articles.title: Using the railway network as a flatbed scanner
articles.titleZh: 把铁路网当成平板扫描仪
articles.author: otherayden

zh.thesis: 用工业线阵相机从火车和渡轮上拍出超宽幅照片，难点不在拍摄，而在后期把速度和视差处理对。
paragraphs: 作者把一台工业线阵相机架在火车窗边，对着窗外连续拍一条一像素宽的竖线，列车前进时再把这些线拼起来，就得到一张全景图。
原理类似老式扫描后背：传感器只有一条线，靠移动来覆盖整个画面。他最初用手机试过，发现速度不均会让画面扭曲，于是改用每秒能读近两万行的 Basler 相机。
硬件只花了两百多美元，麻烦在后期。相机每秒拍四千行，得靠加速度计的数据决定保留哪些线，但加速度计噪声大，积分还会漂移，需要手动猜初速度。
另一个问题是视差：近处的物体移动快，远处的慢。作者用每像素代表的距离来调整，离近处多就强调前景，值大就突出背景，每段画面选好参数后拼起来。
后来他加了彩色相机，又遇到红外污染和红绿蓝通道错位，最后靠滤镜和手动偏移解决。图片太大，JPEG 放不下，只能存成 TIFF，再用 OpenSeadragon 切片放到网页上给人缩放看。
所以这个项目的真正成果不是相机，而是一套折腾出来的后期流程——从加速度积分到视差，每一步都在跟误差作斗争。

en.thesis: Using an industrial line-scan camera from trains and ferries to shoot ultra-wide images; the hard part is postprocessing speed and parallax.
paragraphs: The author mounts an industrial line-scan camera at a train window, capturing a single vertical line of pixels continuously, then stitches the lines together as the train moves, producing a panoramic image.

It's the same idea as old scanning backs: a one-line sensor covers the frame by moving. His first phone test showed uneven speed distorts the picture, so he switched to a Basler camera that reads nearly 19,000 lines a second.

The hardware cost only a couple hundred dollars; the pain was postprocessing. The camera grabs about 4,000 lines per second, so he had to decide which lines to keep, using accelerometer data. But accelerometers are noisy and integration drifts, so he had to guess the starting velocity by eye.

There is also parallax: nearby objects appear to move faster than distant ones. He adjusted the distance each pixel represents — low values emphasize the foreground, high ones bring out the background — and picked parameters for each segment before stitching.

Later he added a color camera, which brought infrared contamination and red-green-blue channel misalignment, fixed with a filter and manual shifting. The images are too big for JPEG, so he saved them as TIFF and tiled them with OpenSeadragon for the browser.
So the project's real output isn't the camera but a postprocessing pipeline he fought through — from acceleration integration to parallax, every step was a battle against error.

articles.title: Chinese carmakers now sell one EV abroad for every two at home
articles.titleZh: 中国车企现在每在国内卖两辆电动汽车，就有一辆销往海外
articles.author: Indranil Ghosh

zh.thesis: 国内销量下滑迫使中国电动汽车大规模出口，且这种趋势是长期的，正在重塑全球市场。
paragraphs: 中国电动汽车制造商在国内失去了买家，却在巴西、泰国和海湾地区找到了新客户。7月份出口创下54万辆的月度纪录，而国内销量约为98万辆，出口与国内销量之比从去年7月的1:5升至1:2。
这种转变并非应对一时困境，而是长期趋势。AutoXing创始人Lei Xing表示，中国车价格低廉、供应充足、技术先进，就像当年的日系车和德系车。Automobility创始人Bill Russo说：“从出口机会变成了出口必需。”
特斯拉也在用出口弥补国内疲软。上海工厂上半年国内销量23.9万辆，出口22.9万辆。除欧洲和北美外的海外市场，中国品牌贡献了EV销量的一半（2023年为四分之一），预计今年该地区EV销量将超过北美。
面对中国车的价格优势，各国设定准入条件。泰国要求获补贴的车企本地建厂抵消进口；巴西将EV进口税提至与燃油车相同；加拿大则降税至6.1%并每年放行4.9万辆。
中国工厂产能过剩，超过100万辆EV待售，这意味着折扣、激励和贬值压力。正如Russo所言：“中国出口汽车的速度超过了海外零售网络的消化能力。”

en.thesis: Falling domestic sales are pushing Chinese EVs abroad at record levels, a structural shift that is reshaping global markets.
paragraphs: Chinese EV makers have lost buyers at home and found new ones in Brazil, Thailand, and the Gulf. July exports hit a record 540,000 vehicles against domestic sales of 980,000, moving the ratio from one exported per five sold at home to one per two.

This is not a response to a bad year but a lasting shift. Lei Xing of AutoXing says the cars are cheap, abundant, and technologically desirable, much like Japanese and German cars were in their export booms. Bill Russo of Automobility puts it starkly: 'We've moved from export opportunity to export necessity.'

Even Tesla leans on exports as home sales weaken: Shanghai delivered 238,955 cars in China in the first half and shipped out 228,994. Outside Europe and North America, Chinese brands now supply half of EV sales, up from a quarter in 2023, and are expected to outsell North America this year.

Facing prices too competitive to shut out, governments are setting terms. Thailand requires subsidized carmakers to build locally to offset imports; Brazil has raised import taxes to match gasoline cars; Canada took the opposite route, slashing a 100% tax to 6.1% and letting in 49,000 cars a year.

Chinese factories outproduce what foreign showrooms can sell, leaving over a million EVs in inventory. That means discounting, incentives, and pressure on resale values. As Russo says, 'We've seen this movie before: China can export vehicles faster than overseas retail networks can absorb them.'

articles.title: Screwworm Infections Get Worse, Government Unleashing Drone Army For Surveillance
articles.titleZh: 螺旋蝇感染恶化，政府动用无人机大军监视
articles.author: Timothy Geigner

zh.thesis: DOGE 砍掉了一项 1.7 亿美元的防疫拨款，结果美国现在要花更多钱应对螺旋蝇疫情，还可能损失近 20 亿美元。
paragraphs: 几个月前，螺旋蝇在得州重现，这是几十年来头一回。原本与墨西哥等国合作的监测项目，因为 DOGE 削减经费而停摆，就像麻疹一样，本来已经消灭的问题又回来了。
螺旋蝇会产卵在牲畜身上，几周就能杀死宿主，墨西哥已有数百人感染。美国这边疫情还在恶化，国土安全部被迫抽调 200 多架边境巡逻无人机，去监测牲畜感染。
美国政府已经花了不少钱：墨西哥投了 2100 万建无菌蝇设施，得州和亚利桑那还要再建两处，各花几千万。而 DOGE 取消的那笔拨款，总共 1.7 亿美元。
更糟的是，据 USDA 估算，如果疫情达到 1976 年的规模，得州经济将损失 18 亿美元。为了省下那点钱，现在花的和可能赔的，都远超当初的预算。

en.thesis: DOGE cut a $170 million disease surveillance grant, and now the US is spending more to fight a screwworm outbreak that threatens nearly $2 billion in damage.
paragraphs: A few months ago screwworm reappeared in Texas for the first time in decades. The program that kept it out, run with countries south of the border, lost funding when DOGE decided it wasn't worth it, so a problem we had eradicated is back, just like measles.

Screwworms lay eggs in livestock and can kill a host in weeks; hundreds of people in Mexico are now infected. On the US side it's getting worse, and Homeland Security has had to pull 200 drones off border patrol to look for infections in animals.
The response is already costing money: $21 million for sterile fly facilities in Mexico, tens of millions for two new ones in Texas and Arizona. The grant DOGE killed was $170 million.
And if the outbreak reaches the scale of the 1976 Texas one, the USDA estimates $1.8 billion in economic damage. So we've likely already spent more than the program cost, and the risk is far bigger.

articles.title: Welcoming First-Year Students with a Wake-Up Call
articles.titleZh: 欢迎新生：一记警钟
articles.author: conversableeconomist

zh.thesis: 美国大学的迎新致辞充满自满，缺乏应有的谦卑和自我怀疑。
paragraphs: 每年秋天，全美大学都自称迎来了史上最优秀、最多样化的新生。安德鲁·德尔班科认为这不太可能。他是哥伦比亚大学美国研究教授，也是国家人文奖章得主。
他在《高等教育纪事报》访谈中指出，严肃的学术工作需要自我怀疑和好奇心。而如今精英机构弥漫着一种优越感——好像他们已掌握所有答案。
早年新英格兰的大学由清教徒创办，校长会告诉新生：“你们都是无用的罪人，全靠上帝恩典。要看到自己的罪与不完美。”今天的致辞则是：“欢迎来到我们伟大的大学，你们是史上最优秀最聪明的学生。”
所以，这种自满情绪是精英机构自己造成的。迎新致辞应当被削弱或调整，谦卑和自省才能回归学术的真正价值。

en.thesis: American college welcoming speeches are full of complacency and lack the humility and self-doubt that serious academic work requires.
paragraphs: Every fall, colleges across the country welcome their 'best-ever, most qualified, most diverse' first-year class. Andrew Delbanco, a Columbia professor and National Humanities Medal winner, finds that unlikely.

In a Chronicle of Higher Education interview, he argues that self-doubt and curiosity are central to serious academic work. But elite institutions now radiate a sense of superiority, as if they have all the answers.

Early Northeastern colleges, founded by Protestants, had presidents who told incoming students: 'You are all worthless sinners, here by God's grace. Hope to see your own sinfulness.' Today's speech: 'Welcome to our great university. You are the best and brightest ever to walk through the gate.'
So the smugness is of the institutions' own making. The welcoming speech should be tempered, and humility should return to the heart of academic life.

articles.title: Why Aren’t Modernist Bridges Awful?
articles.titleZh: 为什么现代主义桥梁不糟糕？
articles.author: Alex Tabarrok

zh.thesis: 公众讨厌现代建筑，却普遍喜欢现代桥梁，原因在于桥梁设计师来自工程系而非建筑系。
paragraphs: 公众不喜欢现代建筑，但对现代桥梁倒没什么恶感。全球最美桥梁榜单里，既有塔桥、布鲁克林桥这些经典，也常常出现巴西的库比契克桥、希腊的里约-安提里奥桥。
几乎没人批评现代桥梁全都很丑，也没有「现代桥梁已不如前辈」的论调。一种解释是，桥梁设计归工程师管，不归建筑师管，美可能只是工程约束的副产品。
但丑桥确实存在，所以不只是工程限制。一个佐证是：建筑杂志《Wallpaper》选出的桥梁大多很丑，和大众喜爱的榜单几乎无重叠。可见丑是一种选择，而非必然。

en.thesis: The public dislikes modern architecture but generally likes modern bridges, and the reason is that bridges are designed by engineers, not architects.
paragraphs: The public dislikes modern architecture but has no such grudge against modern bridges. Lists of the world's most beautiful bridges feature classics like Tower Bridge and the Brooklyn Bridge, but also Brazil's Kubitschek Bridge and Greece's Rio-Antirrio Bridge.

You rarely hear the claim that modern bridges are all ugly, or that they fall short of their predecessors. One explanation is that bridges are designed by engineers, not architects, so beauty may just be a byproduct of engineering constraints.

Ugly bridges do exist though, so constraints alone can't explain it. Tellingly, the bridges chosen by Wallpaper, a magazine about architecture, are mostly ugly, with almost no overlap with the popular lists. So ugliness was a choice, not a necessity.

articles.title: Google has acquired the data of failed US airline Spirit
articles.titleZh: Google 买下了破产航空公司 Spirit 的数据
articles.author: pseudolus

zh.thesis: Google 花 1000 万美元买下 Spirit 的海量数据，主要是为了训练 AI 模型。
paragraphs: 美国廉航 Spirit 在 2020 年新冠疫情中遭受重创，从此一蹶不振，2026 年 5 月永久停飞，进入清算。
法院文件显示，Google 以 1000 万美元赢得竞标，获得超过 1 亿封电子邮件、3000 万条客服电话录音，以及大量 Teams、Oracle 和 SAP 的数据。
这些数据来自破产拍卖，已经去标识化。Google 承诺会清除其中可能存在的个人身份信息，但专家认为，未来通过 AI 提示词泄露个人信息的风险依然存在。
所以，如果你曾乘坐 Spirit 并担心与客服的对话被 Google 知晓，目前看来不必过于忧虑。但拍卖数据训练 AI 的做法，可能引发更多关于隐私的讨论。

en.thesis: Google paid $10 million for Spirit's massive trove of deidentified data, mainly to improve its AI.
paragraphs: US budget carrier Spirit Airlines was hit hard by COVID-19 in 2020 and never recovered, grounding permanently in May 2026 and entering liquidation.
Court documents show Google won an auction for $10 million, buying over 100 million emails, 30 million recorded customer calls, and reams of data from Teams, Oracle, and SAP.
The data was deidentified before the sale, and Google has promised to scrub any personal info it finds. Still, experts warn that personal details could still leak out through future AI prompts.
So if you flew Spirit and worry about Google knowing your call-center chats, you're probably fine for now. But buying bankrupt airlines' data to train AI may open a new privacy debate.

articles.title: Morocco facts of the day, Morocco is not hopeless
articles.titleZh: 摩洛哥每日事实：摩洛哥并非没有希望
articles.author: Tyler Cowen

zh.thesis: 摩洛哥凭借工业升级和区位优势，已成为非洲工业化程度最高的经济体，并成功转向电动汽车和绿色能源。
paragraphs: 几十年里，南非一直是非洲工业化的典范。去年摩洛哥取而代之，成为非洲开发银行工业指数排名第一的经济体。
自 2000 年代中期起，摩洛哥靠地理位置和丰富的磷酸盐储量，与美国、欧盟等 50 多国签了自贸协定，定位成欧洲的「工作台」。
它还抓住了清洁能源转型的机遇。汽车业转向电动车，与雷诺、Stellantis 合作，还建了非洲第一座电池超级工厂。
那座在卡萨布兰卡的工厂年产能 70 吉瓦时，预计能满足欧洲目前市场的三分之一。摩洛哥还批了绿色氢工业园，生产氨、钢铁和工业燃料。
航空制造也是重点，空客、波音、泰雷兹、赛峰都投了进来。到 2024 年，航空出口十年间涨了两倍多，接近 30 亿美元。
所以摩洛哥走的是务实的工业路线：用好地理位置，搭上清洁能源的东风，一步步把产业做起来。

en.thesis: Morocco has become Africa's most industrialized economy by upgrading its industry, diversifying exports, and betting on clean energy and EVs.
paragraphs: For decades South Africa was the model of African industrialization. Last year Morocco took the lead, becoming the top-ranked industrial economy in the African Development Bank's index.
Since the mid-2000s it has leveraged its location and phosphate reserves to sign free trade deals with the US, the EU, and over fifty other countries, positioning itself as a 'workbench' for Europe.
It has also ridden the clean energy shift. Its auto industry is moving to EVs in partnership with Renault and Stellantis, and it hosts Africa's first battery gigafactory.

That factory in Casablanca, with a capacity of 70 gigawatt-hours a year, is expected to supply a third of Europe's current market. The government has also approved a green hydrogen industrial park for ammonia, steel, and industrial fuel.
Aerospace is another focus, with Airbus, Boeing, Thales, and Safran investing. Aerospace exports more than tripled in the decade to 2024, reaching nearly $3 billion.
So Morocco is following a pragmatic industrial path: using its geography and the clean energy wave to build real industries, step by step.

articles.title: Teaching Everyone to Fish for Tokens
articles.titleZh: 教所有人钓 Token
articles.author: Nathan Lambert

zh.thesis: 开源模型的未来取决于 Nvidia 和 Meta 等巨头是否能让开源生态自给自足，否则开源模型将被迫走向长尾。
paragraphs: 人们常拿开源模型和 Linux 相比，但更准确的类比是：开源语言模型（含完整训练配方）相当于开源操作系统，而开权重模型（只有权重和推理代码）类似于基于它安装的软件版本。
权重版本平均寿命很短，但也能用很久，比如很多公司仍在用基于 Llama 3 的工作流。而开源训练配方，如 Ai2 的 Olmo，资源密集但任何公司都能拿来修改并运行出新的权重。
Nvidia 大力投入近乎开源模型，例如 Nemotron 系列，释放所有合法数据和训练代码。它希望无数人能构建 Token 机器，让智能不被垄断，从而带来大量推理需求，带动芯片销售——据说已投入 260 亿美元。
开源 AI 的未来有两个可能：如果 Nvidia 的投入能换来远超成本的芯片需求，生态就能自我维持；否则，开源模型将走向与闭源不同的发展路径，专注效率、可修改性和专业化，成为长尾，比如企业私有化部署的专用代理。
作者认为后一种更可能，因为训练越来越复杂且抽象，社区兴趣转向对 DeepSeek 等模型的后训练微调，而非从头训练。这导致对开源 AI 的投资减少，开源模型的融资变得困难，Nvidia 的策略能否成功悬而未决。
与此同时，Meta 等巨头也通过发布开源权重模型来打击竞争对手（如 Anthropic 和 OpenAI）的收入增长。Nvidia 想教所有人钓鱼，让生态自给自足，而 Meta 则战略性地用 Token 灌满市场，各自在商品化互补品上走了不同的路。

en.thesis: The future of open models hinges on whether giants like Nvidia and Meta can make the open ecosystem self-sustaining, or open models will be pushed to the long tail.
paragraphs: People often compare open models to Linux, but a closer analogy is that open language models (with the full training recipe) are like an open-source operating system, while open-weight models (just weights and inference code) are like a specific software version you install on top.

Weight versions are ephemeral on average but can last long, as with many heavily used software. For instance, many companies still run workflows based on Llama 3. Meanwhile, the open-source recipe, like Ai2's Olmo, is resource-intensive but any company can pick it up, modify it, and run it to produce new weights.

Nvidia is investing heavily in nearly open models, like Nemotron, releasing all legally possible data and training code. It wants a world where countless people can build token machines, preventing intelligence from being monopolized, thus driving massive demand for inference and its chips — reportedly spending $26 billion on this.

The future of open AI has two paths: if Nvidia's investment returns more in chip demand than it costs, the ecosystem can be self-sustaining; otherwise, open models will diverge from closed ones, focusing on efficiency, modifiability, and specialization, becoming a long tail, such as enterprise-specific on-premise agents.

The author thinks the latter is more likely, because training is getting more complex and abstract, and community interest is shifting to post-training fine-tuning of models like DeepSeek rather than full training. This reduces investment in open-source AI, making financing tricky — Nvidia's strategy hangs in the balance.

Meanwhile, giants like Meta also release open-weight models to hurt competitors like Anthropic and OpenAI. Nvidia wants to teach everyone to fish for tokens, so the ecosystem is self-sustaining, while Meta strategically floods the zone with tokens — different ways of commoditizing complements.

articles.title: Where to eat in San Francisco
articles.titleZh: 在旧金山去哪里吃
articles.author: Noah Smith

zh.thesis: 旧金山的美食被低估了，只要你知道去哪找。
paragraphs: 经济学家写美食推荐也算有传统，Tyler Cowen 就写过整本书。我住旧金山十年，试过几百家餐厅，觉得这座城被严重低估了。
很多人说旧金山的餐厅平庸，我不同意。虽然比不上纽约和洛杉矶，但这里的好餐厅远比你听说的多，说它是美食荒漠，那是技术问题。
为什么旧金山不如纽约洛杉矶？首先是城市太小，只有 82 万人，好餐厅数量自然少。租金又贵得离谱，开餐馆难，中档餐厅少得可怜。
再加上市内交通不便，大家只在自己街区吃饭，竞争不激烈，餐厅也就懒得创新。要想改善，得多建房、提速公交、削减官僚程序。
不过我还是找到不少好地方。旧金山的三类餐厅特别强：伪居酒屋、时髦高级餐厅、还有新开的平价小店。
伪居酒屋就是点许多小盘分享，比如墨西哥的 Maria Isabel、泰国的 Prik Hom、中东的 Aziza，还有韩国的 Bansang。时髦高级餐厅像 Mijote，$84 一人，却是全城我最爱的餐厅。
所以别信那些说旧金山美食不行的人。带上这份清单挨家吃过去，你会另有看法。

en.thesis: San Francisco's food is underrated, and the key is knowing where to look.
paragraphs: Economics bloggers recommending restaurants is a tradition - Tyler Cowen wrote a whole book on it. I have lived in San Francisco for a decade, tried several hundred restaurants, and think the city is wildly underrated.

Plenty of people say the dining scene is mediocre, and I disagree. It is not as good as New York or LA, but there are far more good places than you have heard about. Calling it a food desert is a skill issue.

Why does it lag behind New York and LA? First, the city is tiny at 826,000 people, so there are simply fewer good restaurants. Rent is absurdly high, opening a restaurant is hard, and mid-priced options are scarce.

On top of that, transit is bad, so people stay in their own neighborhoods, competition is weak, and restaurants see no reason to innovate. The fixes are more housing, faster transit, and less red tape.
Still, I have found plenty of gems. Three types really shine: pseudo-izakayas, hipster fine dining, and new holes in the wall.

A pseudo-izakaya means small plates to share - Mexican Maria Isabel, Thai Prik Hom, Middle Eastern Aziza, Korean Bansang. For hipster fine dining, Mijote at $84 a head is perhaps my favorite restaurant in the city.
So ignore the naysayers. With this list in hand, you will eat very well in San Francisco.

articles.title: James Joyces’s Baby Impressions and Other “Awkward Pleasures” of Literary Biography
articles.titleZh: 詹姆斯·乔伊斯的婴儿模仿及其他文学传记的「尴尬乐趣」
articles.author: Daisy Hildyard

zh.thesis: 文学传记的魅力在于它那些奇怪的细节和惊喜，但也是充满指责与秘密的尴尬乐趣。
paragraphs: 每个人都涉足传记：致悼词、改简历、说闲话，都得回答 Hermione Lee 在访谈里讨论的问题——人生的形状是什么？成就有哪些要素？出了事，非得找个人来怪罪吗？
她研究传记的方法，是找到「对主体有共鸣的结构」。这种结构里有一种镜像效果：她写别人的生平，而访谈本身也在讲述她这个写生平者的生平。
文学传记是种尴尬的乐趣。你看到乔伊斯模仿婴儿，或托尔斯泰夏天吃马奶酸奶减肥。直到读了塞巴尔德传记，看见他年轻时的照片，才知道他曾在河中站立，手持匕首，你才真正理解他。
这个类型还有实用的价值：知道别的作家怎么追发票、孩子何时午睡。Lee 的传记结合了原始研究与作品解读，经得起重读，她读得那么仔细，那么有想象力。访谈结束，我感受到理解他人生活所需付出的巨大努力。

en.thesis: Literary biography delights in odd details and surprises, but it is an awkward pleasure shot through with blame and secrets.
paragraphs: Everyone dabbles in biography: a eulogy, a CV, gossip — all raise the questions Hermione Lee discusses in her interview. What is the shape of a life? What makes an achievement? When things go wrong, must someone be blamed?
Her approach is to find what she calls 'a structure sympathetic to the subject.' It works like a mirror: she writes lives, and here we watch her talk about that very work.

Literary biography is an awkward pleasure. You catch James Joyce doing baby impressions, or spend the summer with Tolstoy on his horse-yogurt diet. Sebald only made sense once I saw him as a young man in a river, dagger in hand, tanned and muscled.

It is also practical: how writers chased invoices, when their children napped. Lee's biographies blend original research with close reading, and they last. Few read as carefully or as imaginatively. The interview left me awed by what it takes to sincerely understand another life.
